definitions.explanation: A person who stubbornly refuses to change their mind, habits, or ways of doing things. Can be used both critically and with a tone of grudging respect.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{頑固者|がんこもの}だ。
examples.english: My father is a stubborn person.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{頑固者|がんこもの}で、⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦やり{方|かた}→やり方：10532_yarikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{変|か}えない→変える：01089_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: That craftsman is stubborn and won't change his way of doing things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{頑固者|がんこもの}だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{思|おも}っている→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather is stubborn, but he cares about his family more than anyone.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{頑固|がんこ}→頑固：06643_ganko⟧ (stubborn) and ⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧ (person). Often used to describe older men, particularly fathers and grandfathers, and carries a mix of criticism and affection. In the context of craftsmen and artisans, being a {頑固者|がんこもの} can be positive, implying uncompromising dedication to quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {頑固者|がんこもの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{親父|おやじ}: a stubborn old man (father)
- {筋金入|すじがねい}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頑固者|がんこもの}: a thoroughly stubborn person
- ⟦{昔|むかし}ながら→昔ながら：26817_mukashinagara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頑固者|がんこもの}: an old-fashioned stubborn person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}り→意地っ張り：18869_ijippari⟧: obstinate person — more colloquial; implies stubbornness driven by pride or spite
- ⟦{頑固|がんこ}→頑固：06643_ganko⟧な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: stubborn person — the adjective form; more neutral than the compound {頑固者|がんこもの}
- ⟦{強情|ごうじょう}→強情：18243_goujou⟧な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: obstinate person — emphasizes willful refusal to yield
